    [INPUTS]
        <REF> database_name </REF>: str "The database name to assign to the instance."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Assign the database_name parameter to the instance attribute self.database_name. RESULT self.database_name]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
DatabaseProcessor.create_table:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Creates a SQLite table, if it does not already exist, with an id integer primary key column and two dynamically named columns supplied as key1 and key2." create_table]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> table_name </REF>: string "The name of the table to create."
        <REF> key1 </REF>: string "The name of the first custom column, defined as TEXT."
        <REF> key2 </REF>: string "The name of the second custom column, defined as INTEGER."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Connect to the SQLite database using self.database_name and assign the connection to conn. RESULT conn]
            [COMMAND Create a database cursor by calling conn.cursor() and assign it to cursor. RESULT cursor]
            [COMMAND Build create_table_query by interpolating table_name, key1, and key2 into the SQL statement CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {table_name} (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, {key1} TEXT, {key2} INTEGER). RESULT create_table_query]
            [COMMAND Execute the create_table_query using cursor.execute(). RESULT execution_completed]
            [COMMAND Commit the transaction with conn.commit(). RESULT committed]
            [COMMAND Close the database connection with conn.close(). RESULT closed]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
DatabaseProcessor.insert_into_database:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Opens a SQLite database connection, inserts each item from data into the specified table using parameterized name and age values, then commits and closes the connection." insert_into_database]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> table_name </REF>: string "Name of the database table into which rows are inserted."
        <REF> data </REF>: list[dict] "Iterable of dictionaries, each containing 'name' and 'age' keys for one row to insert."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Open a SQLite connection to the database file specified by self.database_name and assign the connection object to conn. RESULT conn]
            [COMMAND Create a cursor from the database connection and assign it to cursor. RESULT cursor]
            [COMMAND For each item in data, construct insert_query by interpolating table_name directly into the SQL string 'INSERT INTO {table_name} (name, age) VALUES (?, ?)'. RESULT insert_query]
            [COMMAND Within the same for loop over data, execute cursor.execute(insert_query, (item['name'], item['age'])) using the current item's name and age as bound parameters. RESULT None]
            [COMMAND Commit the transaction on conn. RESULT None]
            [COMMAND Close the database connection conn. RESULT None]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
DatabaseProcessor.search_database:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Searches the specified SQLite table for rows whose name column matches the provided name and returns them, or returns None if no matching rows are found." search_database]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> table_name </REF>: str "Name of the SQLite table to query; it is interpolated directly into the SQL statement."
        <REF> name </REF>: str "Value to match against the name column in the query."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: list[tuple] | None "List of all matching rows if at least one row is found; otherwise returns None."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Connect to the SQLite database specified by self.database_name. RESULT conn]
            [COMMAND Create a cursor from the database connection conn. RESULT cursor]
            [COMMAND Build the SQL query string using an f-string as SELECT * FROM {table_name} WHERE name = ?, interpolating table_name directly into the query text and leaving the name value as an unbound placeholder. RESULT select_query]
            [COMMAND Execute select_query on the cursor, binding the provided name parameter to the placeholder. RESULT cursor]
            [COMMAND Fetch all remaining rows from the executed query and assign them to result. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Evaluate result for truthiness and select the corresponding return path. RESULT condition_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: result is truthy]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return result unchanged. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: result is falsy]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return None. RESULT None]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
DatabaseProcessor.delete_from_database:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Deletes a row from the specified SQLite table where the name column equals the given name, then commits and closes the database connection." delete_from_database]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> table_name </REF>: str "Name of the SQLite table from which to delete the row."
        <REF> name </REF>: str "Value to match in the name column for deletion."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Connect to the SQLite database at self.database_name using sqlite3.connect(). RESULT conn]
            [COMMAND Create a cursor from the connection with conn.cursor(). RESULT cursor]
            [COMMAND Build the delete query string by interpolating table_name into 'DELETE FROM {table_name} WHERE name = ?' and leaving the '?' placeholder for parameter binding. RESULT delete_query]
            [COMMAND Execute the delete query on the cursor, binding name to the '?' placeholder via cursor.execute(delete_query, (name,)). RESULT None]
            [COMMAND Commit the transaction with conn.commit(). RESULT None]
            [COMMAND Close the database connection with conn.close(). RESULT None]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
